reasoning:
I need to plan the JSON edits now: updating the annotator prompts so each container field (red, green, blue) explicitly states that when a tracked container doesn't move in a step, its field retains the last-frame position, with identity changing only through chain links. I also want to add a policy prompt to the green_container memory requiring all three fields to be rewritten at every step, including a worked example, then apply similar brief guidance to red and blue.

I apply the same wording to blue_container, then update the policy memory for green to specify matching the carried-in position to the nearest container in the first frame and tracking it forward by smallest displacement each step, never jumping straight to the last frame. I also insert a reminder at the start of each field's description that it must be rewritten every step showing containers, regardless of whether that color is named in the goal or whether it moved.

Then I tighten the pointing rules so the policy always points at the value written at the current step after the full chain update, never at the carried-in or just-placed value, making sure the memory update finishes first if the carried-in value still looks stale.

edits.modify_from: [y, x] of the container hiding the green cube.
edits.modify_to: [y, x] of the container hiding the green cube. At every step whose frames show containers, rewrite this field, and likewise red_container and blue_container, whether or not the color is named in the goal and whether or not its container moved.

edits.modify_from: At every later step, match the carried-in position to the nearest container in the FIRST frame shown, then follow it frame to frame, each time choosing the container with the smallest displacement from the previous frame; never match the carried-in position straight to the last frame.
edits.modify_to: At every later step: (1) if the carried value is a cube position (first step with containers), take the container standing on it in the first frame shown; (2) otherwise take the container in the FIRST frame shown nearest the carried value, even if it is 10-15 px away because the glide was already under way; (3) step frame to frame, each time picking the container with the smallest displacement from the one just chosen; (4) write that container's last-frame position. Never match the carried value straight to the last frame. Worked example of the swap trap: carried [131, 115]; first frame has containers at [118, 118] and [113, 162], pick [118, 118]; next frame it is at [99, 134], next at [101, 161]; write [101, 161], although the OTHER container, which came from [113, 162], now stands at [131, 116], almost exactly the carried value. A container standing in the last frame at the carried position is neither for nor against; only the chain decides. Conversely, when no container moves during a step, the chain returns the same container and the value stays (jitter of a few pixels aside).
